question.problem: An arithmetic sequence has the $2$nd term ${a}_{2}=-6$ and the $9$th term ${a}_{9}=-27.$  Calculate the $12$th term.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

 

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$ 

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms ${a}_{2}=-6$ and ${a}_{9}=-27$ and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{9}-{a}_{2}}{9-2} \\  & =\frac{-27-(-6)}{9-2} \\  & =\frac{-21}{7} \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{2}=-6,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{2}$ is $1$ jump after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}+d \\ -6 & ={a}_{1}+(-3) \\ -6 & ={a}_{1}-3 \\ {a}_{1} & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-3+(n-1)\cdot (-3) \\  & =-3n\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can find the $12$th term by substituting $n=12$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12} & =-3(12) \\  & =-36\end{aligned}
$$
